summary_html: CPS **screens out** a report (no investigation) or closes as **unfounded** after minimal review. Federal law (CAPTA) conditions funding on operating screening criteria and recordkeeping; federal reviews (CFSR) assess decision quality.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — screening & intake system requirements  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal performance/quality review of state screening and responses

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the CHINS finding because the parents had cooperated fully and voluntarily obtained services, so there was insufficient evidence that the court's coercive intervention was necessary, noting an informal adjustment was available instead.
key_cases.relevance: Provides the published basis for closing a case as unfounded or unnecessary where the family cooperates.
key_cases.quote: There is insufficient evidence that the coercive intervention of a court is necessary to protect E.K.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the CHINS adjudication, holding the evidence did not show the mother was unlikely to meet the children's needs without the coercive intervention of the court, and it declined to find the appeal moot because of the collateral consequences of a CHINS judgment.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the legal basis for closing or declining a case where the family will accept services without court compulsion.
key_cases.quote: The intrusion of a CHINS judgment, then, must be reserved for families who cannot meet those needs without coercion

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the CHINS adjudication because the Department failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence the third statutory element, that the children needed care the parents were unlikely to provide without the court's coercive intervention.
key_cases.relevance: Where the third element fails, the correct outcome is no court case at all.
key_cases.quote: To prove a child is “in need of services”, the Department must prove three statutory elements by a preponderance of the evidence

timeline_requirements.deadline: 30 days (juvenile court must complete the dispositional hearing)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: The date the court finds that the child is a child in need of services
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Upon a filing of a motion with the court, the court shall dismiss the case without prejudice (Ind. Code § 31-34-19-1(b))
